news.title: Claude may have helped solve the Riemann hypothesis
news.description: The Lean and Mathlib communities indicate that the formal proof of this 167-year-old hypothesis has been verified. This breakthrough could have major implications for AI and mathematics.

news.title: OpenAI calls on rival labs to limit AI training
news.description: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is proposing that AI labs set common limits for training advanced models. He believes safety and monitoring research could fall behind as early as 2027.

news.title: Nvidia’s board chair announces Jensen Huang’s return
news.description: Nvidia’s board chair informed employees of Jensen Huang’s return “after careful consideration,” according to an internal memo.

news.title: Guide: Set up ChatGPT in five minutes
news.description: The guide explains how to enable custom instructions, provide context, and turn on memory so ChatGPT can better adapt to its user.

news.title: Create AI agents with no prior knowledge
news.description: This article explains how to build artificial intelligence agents without prior experience.

news.title: Build an AI agent in minutes with Claude
news.description: The article shows how to quickly build an artificial intelligence agent using Claude.

news.title: Create AI agents with Notion
news.description: The article explains how to create artificial intelligence agents with Notion.

news.title: Anthropic stages a record-breaking IPO
news.description: Anthropic is presented as having completed an IPO that broke all records.

news.title: OpenRouter removes three providers after prompt theft
news.description: OpenRouter removed three providers after researchers discovered prompt theft that allegedly continued for several months at AI hosting companies.

news.title: Ubisoft creates Motherbrain studio dedicated to AI for gameplay
news.description: Ubisoft has created the Motherbrain studio, dedicated to using artificial intelligence in gameplay.

news.title: China fears U.S. AI could expose its nuclear missiles
news.description: According to The New York Times, the Chinese military fears that U.S. artificial intelligence could expose its nuclear missiles.

news.title: Why China won the AI-generated video race
news.description: The article analyzes why China won the race to AI-generated video.

news.title: Microsoft will pay Azure’s top talent more
news.description: Microsoft plans to pay its top Azure employees more and tighten its requirements for other workers.

news.title: Amazon signs deal for Decart’s AI technology and team
news.description: Amazon signed a deal covering Decart’s AI optimization technology and team.

news.title: SpaceX sued over Grok-generated pornographic deepfakes
news.description: Oregon and Virginia are suing SpaceX over AI-generated pornographic deepfakes and safety statements concerning Grok.

news.title: OpenAI’s prompt engineering best practices
news.description: OpenAI presents simple rules and before-and-after examples, including explaining what to do rather than merely stating what not to do.

news.title: A discussion thread examines prompt anti-patterns
news.description: An OpenAI community discussion asks whether adding many instructions can degrade responses, while participants debate the issue.

news.title: Questions about fast charging the Tesla Model Y Premium 2026
news.description: A buyer who reserved a Model Y 2026 asks which home charger to use for the fastest charging at 240 V and whether the Tesla charger has any specific features.

news.title: Tech stocks plunge after three years of gains
news.description: The three major indexes fell sharply Friday, with the Nasdaq dropping more than 5% and wiping out all its 2026 gains. Concerns about Anthropic’s IPO, tighter regulation and inflation are driving the decline, which could also represent an overdue reset.

news.title: eBay sellers try to capitalize on enthusiasm around Anthropic
news.description: Anthropic’s IPO did not prevent a sharp drop in its stock on the second day of trading. eBay sellers offering products presented as official include sweatshirts priced at $1,800 and a Claude tote bag at $100.

news.title: OpenAI agents complete half of research tasks
news.description: OpenAI agents complete nearly 50% of tasks that would take a researcher two to four hours, up from 25% in March. Researchers use an average equivalent of $2,400 worth of agents per day.

news.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Accounting to automate bookkeeping
news.description: ChatGPT can connect to companies’ accounting software to automate bank reconciliation, invoice entries, detection of missing or duplicate transactions, and preparation for closings and audits.

news.title: ChatGPT adds live dictation and collaborative spaces
news.description: Live voice dictation is coming to ChatGPT apps. Plus subscribers also get ChatGPT Space, which creates collaborative pages and presentations updated using connected tools.

news.title: Automate sales prospecting
news.description: The article presents methods for automating sales prospecting.

news.title: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia employees
news.description: Nvidia’s CEO returned to headquarters in Santa Clara, where employees welcomed him with cheers and chants. He apologized for the turbulence and promised to be “a better CEO the second time around.”

news.title: Jensen Huang’s victory tour revelations on CNBC
news.description: This article revisits the biggest revelations from Jensen Huang’s victory tour with Trump on CNBC.

news.title: Trump wants corporate America to remember who is in charge
news.description: The article reports that Trump wants corporate America to remember who is in charge.

news.title: Jensen Huang is worth $1 trillion to Nvidia
news.description: Jensen Huang’s value to Nvidia amounts to $1 trillion, something the board could not ignore.

news.title: Tesla says the new FSD version is 25 times safer
news.description: Tesla has begun rolling out Full Self-Driving v15 and claims the system handles critical situations 25 times better. The update notably adds a real-time view of the vehicle’s intentions, but the system remains supervised.

news.title: Meta’s AI chief announces the arrival of superintelligence
news.description: Alexandr Wang, Meta’s AI chief, says superintelligence is coming and urges humanity to reject any transfer of control to AI. He is particularly concerned about the automation of AI research and the recursive improvement of models.

news.title: U.S. intelligence warns of new technology outages
news.description: U.S. intelligence director Jay Clayton warns that Americans should expect more disruptions and technology outages. The warning comes after several incidents involving system and network upgrades.

news.title: CrowdStrike acquires Zscaler for $43.9 billion
news.description: CrowdStrike reached an all-stock agreement to acquire Zscaler in a transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion. Zscaler is expected to bring nearly 8,000 customers, while CrowdStrike anticipates about $1 billion in additional annual revenue.

news.title: Sierra doubles its valuation to $30 billion in six months
news.description: The article reports that Sierra doubled its valuation to $30 billion in six months, driven by demand for AI in customer experience.

news.title: Dutch privacy authority advises against “perverse glasses”
news.description: The Dutch data protection authority is urging consumers not to buy the “perverse glasses.”

news.title: Google’s quantum chip surpasses classical limits in an impossible game
news.description: The article presents the results of a Google quantum chip that surpasses the limits of classical computers in a game described as “impossible.”

news.title: Google’s AI search monetization costs Apple revenue
news.description: The article claims that Google’s failure to monetize AI search is causing Apple to lose revenue.

news.title: Chips withstand space, but their funding is uncertain
news.description: The article examines chips’ ability to survive in the space environment and questions the viability of their funding.

news.title: Perplexity and intelligence
news.description: The article titled “Perplexity and Intelligence” concerns the links between Perplexity and intelligence.

news.title: Z.ai launches GLM-5.4, its first Loop Transformer model
news.description: Z.ai has launched GLM-5.4, its first model based on the Loop Transformer architecture.

news.title: AI assistant extensions pose risks to private data
news.description: An audit conducted before installation flagged potential privacy violations in approximately 55% of more than 500 marketplace skills handling personal information.

news.title: AI data center planning can cut costs by 6.5%
news.description: Planning that combines multiple chip types and different AI workloads across sites and schedules could reduce daily costs by about 6.5% while staying within local power-grid constraints.

news.title: U.S. election prediction markets slow down
news.description: Prediction markets generated $2.7 billion in transactions for this year’s U.S. elections, compared with $8.5 billion in 2024, according to an analysis by the Pew Research Center.

news.title: Shorter, consistent prompts make models more reliable
news.description: Prompts that accumulate contradictory rules give the model two commands at once. The article recommends removing contradictions and stating what the model should do instead of multiplying prohibitions.

news.title: Claude’s prompt engineering best practices
news.description: This guide presents essential techniques and common mistakes, with a section devoted to positive instructions rather than avoidance-based wording.

news.title: Google’s prompt design strategies for Gemini
news.description: Google details clear instructions, examples and constraints, as well as how to prioritize rules when they conflict.

news.title: When negative prompts are still useful
news.description: Virtualization Review explains when an instruction such as “avoid this” may still be relevant and why too many constraints produce the opposite effect.

news.title: A new Tesla owner worries about range on road trips
news.description: A new owner living in the southwestern United States is planning several Tesla trips but is concerned about Supercharger availability in some areas.

news.title: A Tesla makes an intelligent lane change earlier than expected
news.description: A driving observation reports an automated lane change approximately 100 to 200 meters before the turnoff. This behavior could reduce lane changes and last-minute slowdowns.

news.title: Tesla’s Cybercab is now available by invitation
news.description: The Cybercab has been announced as available by invitation.

news.title: Speaker considers Tesla’s future model insufficiently desirable
news.description: One participant believes wealthy people would not want to be seen in this plastic vehicle and instead cites the Roadster as an attractive model, if it ever materializes.

news.title: An owner uses public NEMA 14-50 outlets to charge their Tesla
news.description: After buying their first Tesla in 2023, an owner discovered NEMA 14-50 outlets in a public park they visited daily. The outlets had originally been installed for food trucks.

news.title: Owner requests a light in the Tesla charging port
news.description: An owner would like a light in the charging port to make it easier to position the connector when it is raining, without having to find the opening by touch.

news.title: Tesla could insure autonomous vehicles itself
news.description: Tesla has long considered becoming the insurer of fully autonomous vehicles, while potentially partnering with existing insurance companies in heavily regulated markets.

news.title: A buyer receives a new Tesla with outdated software
news.description: An owner of a Model Y 2027 says they asked whether the software was up to date at delivery and received an affirmative answer. Their one-month FSD trial began immediately afterward.

news.title: Forum member defends electric vehicles against hybrids
news.description: One participant says they would not choose any hybrid for a road trip over their Model 3 Performance or Cybertruck. They say they have been taking fully electric trips for a long time.

news.title: User reminds others that FSD must be actively supervised
news.description: A user says they would only feel unsafe with FSD if they were not actively supervising it. To them, that means staying attentive to the road and keeping their hands ready to take control.

news.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Mini, a model that runs on Mac
news.description: Inkling 2 Mini is a general-purpose multimodal model compact enough to run on a Mac with at least 32 GB of RAM. It uses, among other things, a new recurrent transformer architecture and joins the few American open-weight models competing with China’s lead.

news.title: Create a 60-second KPI recap video with Claude
news.description: The tutorial explains how to connect a data source in Claude, create a “Visual short” artifact and generate a summary video for management. It recommends checking indicator definitions, filters and periods before approving the result.

news.title: Notion recommends a shared context system to automate work
news.description: Notion co-founder Akshay Kothari advises organizations to create a shared space containing their information and processes. He says this “context system” would allow agents to learn continuously and take over routine tasks, while employees supervise their work.

news.title: AI demand threatens to cause a printed circuit board shortage
news.description: Demand for AI servers is straining the supply of printed circuit boards and displacing automotive, medical and industrial orders. A significant improvement in supply is not expected before mid-2028.

news.title: Ubuntu targets 2028 for its immutable desktop
news.description: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for Core Desktop, with the provisional goal of making it the default download in version 30.04. The system is based on isolated snap packages and atomic updates, while traditional Ubuntu will remain available.

news.title: SAP details its strategy for an autonomous enterprise
news.description: SAP’s AI chief explains how the company manages costs, governance and models for its autonomous enterprise concept and AI agents. SAP combines daily usage limits, default models and centralized controls, but still struggles to link token consumption directly to financial value.

news.title: Cloud monitoring can miss AI failures
news.description: An AI service can remain online while producing incorrect answers, violating policies or generating unexpected costs. Teams must monitor output quality, agent behavior and spending, and establish processes for restoring reliable behavior.

news.title: Google rolls out ambient networking for GKE
news.description: Google announced general availability of ambient networking for Google Kubernetes Engine, with a sidecarless service mesh architecture. It separates networking functions from application workloads to reduce resource consumption and management complexity.

news.title: AWS tests centralized Internet firewall controls
news.description: AWS Network Firewall can now apply centralized filtering rules directly to VPC Internet gateways without changing routing or architecture. The preview includes built-in NAT and automatically extends policies to new VPCs and subnets.

news.title: GitHub releases Enterprise Server 3.23 release candidate
news.description: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 adds improved filtering in GitHub Projects, AI secret detection in isolated environments and expanded malware detection. The update also brings several improvements to Dependabot, OAuth tokens and cluster configuration.

news.title: AWS adds an API to instantly estimate workload costs
news.description: The new Pricing Calculator API estimates up to 500 usage lines per request based on public or customer-specific rates. It allows infrastructure price calculations to be integrated directly into existing tools.

news.title: AWS DevOps Agent expands its conversational capabilities
news.description: AWS DevOps Agent can now directly execute GitHub and PagerDuty actions from Claude Code, Slack and Microsoft Teams.

news.title: Google Quantum AI observes contextuality up to 105 qubits
news.description: Google’s Willow quantum processor exceeded classical limits in the Mermin-Peres magic square game, with a success rate of 98.3%.

news.title: Windows hotpatch causes application failures
news.description: Microsoft acknowledged application failures after the November hotpatch for Windows 11 and provided a Registry workaround that requires a restart.

news.title: Tesla rolls out version 15 of its FSD autonomous driving system
news.description: Version 15 notably improves sign detection, pothole handling and speed in school zones. It also adds live visualization and slowing at speed cameras, and has begun rolling out.

news.title: Neuralink expands clinical trials to Canada and the United Kingdom
news.description: Neuralink has increased the frequency of procedures and expanded its clinical trials to Canada and the United Kingdom. Early participants are holding video calls with new participants to help them use the technology.

news.title: AI in biology also depends on the quality of measured data
news.description: Progress in AI for biology will depend not only on the volume of data, but also on what is measured and its quality. Systematically incomplete measurements will probably not allow researchers to fully understand complex biological systems.

news.title: Developer programs an FPGA to run a language model
news.description: A developer used “vibe coding” to run a language model on an FPGA. The experiment shows what becomes possible with a large token budget and suitable problems.

news.title: AI models can serve as informal proof checkers
news.description: This article examines the use of System One models as informal proof checkers. These methods can complement formal approaches to increase confidence in agentic software development workflows.

news.title: Superintelligence is more likely to arrive in 2029 than 2027
news.description: The author estimates that the industry is about 60% of the way toward superintelligence compared with 2022. In their view, it will probably arrive in 2029 rather than 2027, and work on longer-term timelines should not be neglected.

news.title: An associate of Alice Huang is accused of shipping Nvidia chips to China
news.description: Li Ming allegedly played a central role in a network of companies smuggling restricted Nvidia chips into China. He was indicted for fraud in February 2025 in a case related to the alleged transshipment, which is still ongoing.

news.title: More than 95% of new Chinese micro-dramas are produced with AI
news.description: More than 95% of new micro-dramas released in China are now made with AI.

news.title: A researcher compresses one billion bytes of Wikipedia with a Transformer model
news.description: A researcher compressed one billion bytes of Wikipedia into 105,388,353 bytes. The package includes the offline-trained weights and decoder for a 12-layer Transformer with 163 million parameters.

news.title: A team deploys more than 100 pull requests to production in one week
news.description: Although many of these pull requests were simple, their volume reflects how the fundamentals of software development are evolving.

news.title: Autonomous media could transform the industry in 2027
news.description: AI-generated voices and videos are becoming increasingly convincing. This evolution will have major implications for the media industry.

news.title: Researchers reveal a sensitive data leak in the AI supply chain
news.description: The researchers placed two million canaries in the AI supply chain. They discovered an ecosystem exposing large amounts of highly sensitive data.

news.title: Journalist discovers that becoming a real estate agent is far too easy
news.description: After covering real estate for years, James Rodriguez took the training and passed the exam to become an agent. He found that the preparation mainly taught the rules, without really teaching negotiation or how to do the job.

news.title: Copper’s decline raises fears of a weakening U.S. economy
news.description: Copper, considered a quiet indicator of economic conditions, has fallen 17% from its recent peak. The decline is worrying analysts about the strength of the U.S. economy.

news.title: BNP Paribas forecasts three Fed rate hikes
news.description: BNP Paribas’ chief U.S. economist forecasts three 25-basis-point hikes at the December, January and March meetings. The bank says the labor market could withstand them, but AI-related stocks could suffer.

news.title: U.S. futures rebound alongside technology stocks
news.description: U.S. stock futures rose Monday as technology stocks recovered after the sharp sell-off the previous week.

news.title: Divorcees build their own AI tools to manage separation
news.description: People going through divorce are using AI to reduce the financial and emotional burdens of separation. They are developing their own solutions as the legal sector evolves slowly.

news.title: Caltech students ease conflict over AI in mathematics
news.description: After calls to cancel their AI-using “mathathon,” Caltech students removed Anthropic as a sponsor, deleted unsolved problems and rewarded clear explanations.

news.title: Amazon’s CFO leads a $220 billion investment in AI
news.description: John Felton is overseeing Amazon’s $220 billion AI deployment as investors worry about the returns on that spending. The article examines his background and how he is running the program.

news.title: Middle-management jobs persist in services
news.description: While some technology executives question the usefulness of middle managers, these roles remain common in retail, hospitality and other services. Some of these managers earn six figures without an office or a suit.

news.title: Five scenarios could let Jensen Huang retake control of Nvidia
news.description: The path for Nvidia’s former CEO to return to power is narrowing but remains open. He could, among other options, challenge the board through a proxy fight or a special meeting.

news.title: Pay-what-you-want coffee experiment draws few customers but generous donations
news.description: Few customers showed up for Poorboy Coffee’s pay-what-you-want experiment. Those who came were generous, with some donating as much as $50.

news.title: High interest rates worsen student-loan repayment problem
news.description: A major student-loan repayment problem is drawing the attention of both U.S. political parties: high interest rates.

news.title: Search for an automated utopia leads to mediocre content
news.description: The author says they searched for an automated utopia but found only “roboslop,” low-quality automated content.

news.title: Trump wants Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia
news.description: Scott Bessent believes Jensen Huang could be a good fit to return to his position at Nvidia, while Donald Trump also wants him back.

news.title: Automated-system problem delays hundreds of Delta flights
news.description: Hundreds of Delta flights were delayed nationwide following a problem affecting an automated system.

news.title: French hunting billionaire takes his fight international
news.description: After a tax defeat in California, a French hunting billionaire is expanding his fight worldwide.

news.title: County at the heart of data-center boom pauses new projects
news.description: The U.S. county at the center of the data-center boom is putting new projects on hold.

news.title: Elon Musk warns data-center delays threaten AI companies
news.description: Elon Musk believes delays in data centers could leave AI companies short of cash.

news.title: Investors hesitate as AI-related stocks tumble
news.description: The massive sell-off in AI-related stocks is worrying investors. Five professionals assess whether it is a buying opportunity or a trap closing in.

news.title: Intuit asks Mailchimp employees to support one another after acquisition
news.description: Intuit is asking Mailchimp employees to “take care of one another” after the announcement of its acquisition by Bending Spoons.

news.title: Dries Van Noten’s $400 fragrances become a status symbol
news.description: Dries Van Noten’s $400 fragrances are being presented as the latest social-status symbol. The author tested five and ranked them from worst to best.

news.title: Warren Buffett ends his career in classic style
news.description: Warren Buffett is preparing to conclude his career in a style characteristic of him.

news.title: Flight searches for Miami surge as GTA 6 anticipation builds
news.description: Searches for flights to Miami are rising as travelers seek to visit the real-life “Vice City” from GTA 6.

news.title: The Binding of Isaac removes AI-generated music after controversy
news.description: Developer Nicalis removed AI-generated music from the game after players discovered Suno metadata in the audio files. The incident is a reminder that files can reveal the origin of creative content.

news.title: SWE-CoWork exposes the limits of coding agents against demanding requirements
news.description: The SWE-CoWork benchmark evaluates coding agents on 101 tasks whose requirements are distributed across multiple colleagues and documents. The best models passed about 63% of key tests but fewer than 8% of complete tasks, while 31% of requirements marked complete failed testing.

news.title: AI agents also advance in writing, design and freelance work
news.description: Ethan Mollick says models are improving in fields where quality must be judged by humans, such as writing, design and freelance assignments. The share of freelance-style projects completed at a professional level reportedly rose from 3.75% with Opus 4.5 to 41.25% with Fable 5.2.

news.title: Palo Alto Networks acquires Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
news.description: Palo Alto Networks has agreed to acquire Applied Compute, a company that helps businesses customize and run open models. The all-stock transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of Palo Alto Networks’ fiscal 2027.

news.title: Cybersecurity leaders anticipate more sophisticated attacks
news.description: More than 50 AI and security executives expect increasingly sophisticated and disruptive cyberattacks over the next 18 months.

news.title: U.S. Treasury does not rule out Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
news.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he could not rule out Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia. The company, however, said it had no plans to do so.

news.title: Gemini’s image tools create, edit and animate images
news.description: Gemini’s image tools can turn a prompt into an image, edit an existing image from a natural-language description and create an approximately three-second looping GIF.

news.title: Mistral Vibe Desktop launches multiple coding agents on Mac and Windows
news.description: Mistral AI launched Vibe Desktop, a native macOS and Windows application that can run multiple coding agents in parallel. The download is free, and Linux is coming soon.

news.title: Discount AI API providers stole keys and read queries
news.description: A Dragos investigation reveals that three API providers stole AWS keys and accessed their clients’ queries after a fake-query campaign. OpenRouter removed these providers and revoked the privacy label for 125 endpoints.

news.title: MIT lands an insect robot on a sunflower
news.description: A 1.29-gram flying robot equipped with its own sensors and processor navigated around plants before landing on a sunflower. It was still guided by a human using a joystick.

news.title: Nick Bostrom estimates AI could extend life expectancy to 1,400 years
news.description: Nick Bostrom estimates that, without aging, human life expectancy could reach 1,200 to 1,400 years. In his view, AI could accelerate research into aging.

news.title: Boston Dynamics will test its Atlas humanoid in chip factories
news.description: GlobalFoundries already uses the Spot robot at several sites, where it has carried out more than 90,000 inspections with a 99% success rate. The manufacturer will test Atlas beginning in early 2027, a first for a humanoid in semiconductor manufacturing.

news.title: AI data centers sharply worsen carbon emissions
news.description: According to a Harvard study cited in an opinion piece, the 400 largest U.S. data centers get 54% of their electricity from fossil fuels and emit 25.7 million tons of CO₂ per year. Anthropic’s future data centers could emit nearly 20 megatons annually.

news.title: METR warns of AI advancing faster than the tests
news.description: According to METR, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are rapidly improving on research tasks but becoming difficult to evaluate. The organization cannot rule out a dangerous acceleration, while noting that the tests could overestimate their capabilities.

news.title: Localcode offers a fully local open-source coding agent on Mac
news.description: Localcode lets users run an autonomous programming assistant on a Mac with a single command, without sending data to the cloud. The project is still young and its documentation is limited.

news.title: Flat robots automatically park cars by sliding underneath them
news.description: Two Hyundai WIA robots can slide under a car, lift it by its wheels, and move it sideways to park it. The technology could increase parking capacity by 20% to 50%.

news.title: Devin Desktop becomes free for entire teams
news.description: According to the AI Secret newsletter, Cognition’s Devin Desktop coding agent is now reportedly free for complete teams. The terms and limits of the offer have not been specified.

news.title: Perplexity launches Monitor API for continuous web monitoring
news.description: Monitor API regularly monitors the web and alerts an AI agent only when a relevant change appears. An in-house model is tasked with filtering out the noise.

news.title: Hermes Agent comes to Microsoft Teams
news.description: Hermes Agent, described as OpenRouter’s most widely used open agent, is available in Teams, the Microsoft Store, and Azure. It can analyze documents, perform financial analysis, and sort emails from a conversation.

news.title: Google opens Genie 4, its interactive-world generator
news.description: Google AI Ultra subscribers can create and edit explorable worlds in real time using simple text, with sound that adapts to the scenes. An agent helps build the worlds, and a gallery lets users share their creations.

news.title: Waymo suspends highway rides after California ban
news.description: California’s DMV deemed Waymo’s driverless highway rides dangerous after three vehicles entered a closed construction zone. Waymo suspended highway rides in all its cities.

news.title: China trains Xing4, a 285-billion-parameter model without Nvidia
news.description: The TeleChat team trained Xing4 on 8,192 Huawei Ascend 910C chips using the MindSpore framework. The model illustrates China’s efforts to train large models despite U.S. restrictions, but its actual performance remains poorly documented.

news.title: Nvidia halts shipments of Hopper chips to China
news.description: Nvidia confirmed that no more licensed Hopper chips would be shipped to China and that these sales were disappearing from its forecasts. The decision further deepens the separation between the U.S. and Chinese AI ecosystems.

news.title: U.S. investigates Nvidia chip sales to China
news.description: U.S. authorities are investigating Megaspeed, a Singaporean cloud company suspected of circumventing export controls to China. The U.S. Treasury is also asking Nvidia who was aware of these sales.

news.title: AI coding agents complete fewer than one in ten tasks in real-world environments
news.description: In a simulated developer office with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, Opus 5.5 and Astra complete fewer than 10% of tasks. They remain effective on clear, isolated assignments but lose track in a chaotic environment.

news.title: U.S. banks tighten restrictions on AI agents
news.description: Wells Fargo warns that using an AI agent is at the customer’s own risk, while JPMorgan Chase already bans agents that use its credentials. Other banks and companies are also blocking certain actions performed by bots.

news.title: Data centers become a focal point of opposition to Big Tech
news.description: Journalist Paris Marx considers the growth of data centers unsustainable because of their impact on electricity bills, water, and noise. In his view, this opposition may have influenced the latest U.S. midterm elections.

news.title: Google search slowdown weighs on Apple’s revenue
news.description: Google’s stock fell 18% after its advertising revenue growth slowed, partly due to the success of its AI answers. Apple, which receives a share of revenue generated through Safari, saw its services growth decline from 12% to 10%.
